items.name: avatar-avatar-group
items.title: Avatar: Avatar Group
items.description:
Use the `AvatarGroup` component to overlap a set of avatars. Each avatar is clipped around the avatar above it, leaving a transparent gap instead of a background-colored ring.

`topmost` chooses which avatar stays whole. It defaults to `last`, which keeps a trailing `<AvatarGroupCount>` intact. Use `topmost="first"` when the first avatar should lead the stack.

Adjust the overlap with `--avatar-overlap` and the cut gap with `--avatar-gap`:

```tsx
<AvatarGroup className="[--avatar-overlap:0.625rem] [--avatar-gap:0.125rem]">
  <Avatar>...</Avatar>
  <Avatar>...</Avatar>
  <AvatarGroupCount>+3</AvatarGroupCount>
</AvatarGroup>
```

items.name: avatar-badge
items.title: Avatar: Badge
items.description:
Use the `AvatarBadge` component to add a badge to the avatar. The badge sits at the inline end and bottom of the avatar, so it moves to the bottom left in RTL layouts.

The image and fallback are clipped around the badge, leaving a transparent gap instead of painting a background-colored ring. That means the badge stays legible on any surface without extra classes.

Use a theme token such as `bg-success` to set the badge color.

```tsx
<Avatar>
  <AvatarImage
    src="https://images.pexels.com/photos/1681010/pexels-photo-1681010.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=256&h=256&fit=crop"
    alt="John Doe"
  />
  <AvatarFallback>JD</AvatarFallback>
  <AvatarBadge className="bg-success" />
</Avatar>
```

items.name: bubble-variants
items.title: Bubble: Variants
items.description:
Use `variant` to change the visual treatment of the bubble.

| Variant     | Description                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `default`   | A strong primary bubble, usually for the current user. |
| `secondary` | The standard neutral bubble for conversation content.  |
| `muted`     | A lower-emphasis bubble for quiet supporting content.  |
| `tinted`    | A subtle primary-tinted bubble.                        |
| `outline`   | A bordered bubble for secondary or rich content.       |
| `ghost`     | Unframed content for assistant text or rich content.   |
| `error`     | A error bubble for error or failed actions.            |

A bubble sizes to its content, up to 80% of the container width. The `ghost` variant removes the max-width so assistant text and rich content can span the full row.

items.name: calendar-selected-date-with-timezone
items.title: Calendar: Selected Date (With TimeZone)
items.description:
The Calendar component accepts a `timeZone` prop to ensure dates are displayed and selected in the user's local timezone.

**Note:** If you notice a selected date offset (for example, selecting the 20th highlights the 19th), make sure the `timeZone` prop is set to the user's local timezone.

**Why client-side?** The timezone is detected using `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` inside a `useEffect` to ensure compatibility with server-side rendering. Detecting the timezone during render would cause hydration mismatches, as the server and client may be in different timezones.

items.name: carousel-autoplay
items.title: Carousel: Autoplay
items.description:
Add `CarouselAutoplay` to advance the slides on a timer. It renders the pause and play button that moving content needs, waits while the carousel is hovered or focused, and stops when someone navigates. Under reduced motion it starts paused. Combine it with `loop` so the carousel keeps going past the last slide. Pair it with `CarouselIndicator` and the current dot fills over `delay`, so readers can see when the next slide comes in; the fill holds while autoplay waits and turns solid once it stops.

```tsx
<Carousel aria-label="Highlights" loop>
  <CarouselSlides>...</CarouselSlides>
  <CarouselAutoplay delay={2000} />
  <CarouselIndicator />
</Carousel>
```

items.name: carousel-lightbox
items.title: Carousel: With lightbox
items.description:
`Carousel` and `Lightbox` share the same `value` and `onValueChange` contract, so one state can drive both. Wrap each slide's image in a `LightboxTrigger`. Selecting a slide opens the viewer at that photo, and closing it leaves the carousel on the photo last shown. While the viewer covers the carousel, a new `value` moves the carousel without animation, so it is already at rest when the close transition measures where to land.

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = React.useState(0);

<Lightbox value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
  <Carousel aria-label="Photos" value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
    <CarouselSlides>
      <CarouselSlide>
        <LightboxTrigger index={0}>...</LightboxTrigger>
      </CarouselSlide>
    </CarouselSlides>
  </Carousel>
  <LightboxContent aria-label="Photos">...</LightboxContent>
</Lightbox>;
```

items.description:

```tsx
// 33% of the carousel width.

  <CarouselSlides>
    <CarouselSlide className="basis-1/3">...</CarouselSlide>
    <CarouselSlide className="basis-1/3">...</CarouselSlide>

  </CarouselSlides>
</Carousel>
```

  <CarouselSlides>
    <CarouselSlide className="md:basis-1/2 lg:basis-1/3">...</CarouselSlide>
    <CarouselSlide className="md:basis-1/2 lg:basis-1/3">...</CarouselSlide>

items.name: carousel-spacing
items.title: Carousel: Spacing
items.description:
Set the space between slides with the `--carousel-gap` custom property on `Carousel`. The default is `--spacing(4)`. Slide sizes set with `basis` stay exact at any gap.

```tsx
<Carousel aria-label="Products" className="[--carousel-gap:--spacing(1)]">
  <CarouselSlides>
    <CarouselSlide>...</CarouselSlide>
    <CarouselSlide>...</CarouselSlide>
  </CarouselSlides>
</Carousel>
```

```tsx
// A wider gap on larger screens.
<Carousel
  aria-label="Products"
  className="[--carousel-gap:--spacing(2)] md:[--carousel-gap:--spacing(4)]"
>
  ...
</Carousel>
```

items.name: combobox-async-search
items.title: Combobox: Async search
items.description:
Open the project picker and type a query. This story simulates a delayed request locally, cancels obsolete requests, and hides stale results while searching. The first arriving match is highlighted; use arrow keys and Enter to choose it. Search for a missing project to see the empty state, then clear the query to restore the longer list and its thin scrollbar.

The flush search header stays outside the scrolling list and retains its separator. Header height follows our search sizing on desktop and mobile; the list uses the space left by the actual header rather than subtracting a fixed height. For a real service, cancel the request and use `filter={null}` when the service already filters results.

Show a centered spinner while results are pending, with an accessible search status. Use `ComboboxStatus` for loading or error announcements and `ComboboxEmpty` for a completed search with no matches. Keep Status mounted while the popup is open and update its children; hiding or conditionally mounting the live region can prevent announcements. The list's `aria-busy` communicates that results are still arriving.

items.name: drawer-custom-sizes
items.title: Drawer: Custom Sizes
items.description:
A vertical drawer sizes itself to its content and is capped at `calc(100dvh - 6rem)` by default. A side drawer spans `75%` of the viewport width, or `24rem` on larger screens.

To customize the height of a vertical drawer, use the `h-*` and `max-h-*` utilities on `DrawerPanel`.

To customize the width of a side drawer, use the `w-*` and `max-w-*` utilities on `DrawerPanel`.

When the same component renders in multiple directions, scope an override to one axis using the `data-[swipe-axis=*]` variants.

To make a region of the drawer scrollable, make the scroll container a flex item. Avoid `h-full`, which does not resolve inside a content-sized drawer.

```tsx
<DrawerPanel className="h-[50vh]">
```

```tsx
<DrawerPanel className="w-96">
```

```tsx
<DrawerPanel className="data-[swipe-axis=y]:max-h-[50vh] data-[swipe-axis=x]:w-96">
```

```tsx
<DrawerPanel>
  <DrawerHeader>...</DrawerHeader>
  <DrawerContent>{/* Scrollable content */}</DrawerContent>
  <DrawerFooter>...</DrawerFooter>
</DrawerPanel>
```

items.name: drawer-snap-points
items.title: Drawer: Snap Points
items.description:
Use `snapPoints` to snap a drawer to preset heights. Numbers between `0` and `1` represent fractions of the viewport. Numbers greater than `1` are treated as pixel values. String values support `px` and `rem` units. Snap points apply to vertical drawers.

Track the active snap point with the controlled `snapPoint` and `onSnapPointChange` props. At the full snap point, the drawer gets a `data-expanded` attribute you can style with the `data-expanded:` variant.

items.name: drawer-styling
items.title: Drawer: Styling
items.description:
The drawer exposes CSS variables for style-level customization. Set the sizing variables on `DrawerPanel`. Set the overlay variable on `[data-slot=drawer-overlay]` in your CSS.

| Variable                       | Default                      | Description                                                             |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--drawer-inset`               | `0px`                        | Floats the drawer from the viewport edges.                              |
| `--drawer-bleed-background`    | `var(--color-surface-modal)` | Fills the gap behind the drawer on swipe overshoot.                     |
| `--drawer-overlay-min-opacity` | `0`                          | Minimum overlay opacity. Defaults to `0.5` when snap points are active. |

The drawer also sets data attributes you can target with variants such as `data-[swipe-direction=down]:` on `DrawerPanel`, or `group-data-[swipe-axis=y]/drawer-popup:` on its descendants.

| Attribute                 | Values                        | Set when                              |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `data-swipe-direction`    | `up`, `right`, `down`, `left` | Always.                               |
| `data-swipe-axis`         | `x`, `y`                      | Always.                               |
| `data-snap-points`        | Present                       | The drawer has snap points.           |
| `data-expanded`           | Present                       | The drawer is at the full snap point. |
| `data-swiping`            | Present                       | A swipe is in progress.               |
| `data-nested-drawer-open` | Present                       | A nested drawer is open on top.       |

items.name: field-validation-and-errors
items.title: Field: Validation And Errors
items.description:
- Add `invalid` to `Field` (Base UI `Field.Root`) to switch the entire block into an error state. Controls inside it receive `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid` automatically.

- `FieldError` takes its messages as `errors`, a list of strings. In a TanStack Form, use `field.Field` and `field.FieldError` from the [Form](/docs/components/form) module instead: they bind `invalid`, `touched`, and `dirty`, and decode the field's errors, including Effect Schema issues, into messages.

- `FieldDescription` renders only while the field is valid. Compose it with `FieldError` in the same field: the error replaces the helper information, including its accessible description. This also applies to `FieldSet` and descriptions inside `FieldContent`.

- Render `FieldError` immediately after the control or inside `FieldContent` to keep error messages aligned with the field.

```tsx
<Field invalid>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <Input type="email" />
  <FieldDescription>We will use this to contact you.</FieldDescription>
  <FieldError match>Enter a valid email address.</FieldError>
</Field>
```

items.description:
One Effect Schema validates a contact form: a trimmed name, an email pattern, a minimum message length, and a terms checkbox that must be checked. Submit the empty form to see the messages, then fix a value to clear its error as you type. The terms checkbox shows no message: it turns invalid and shakes with its label, and screen readers still announce the schema's message.

Each `form.AppField` renders a bound field: `TextField`, `TextareaField`, `SwitchField`, and `CheckboxField`. The description is removed while the field is invalid and returns when validation clears, so helper information and errors never appear together. `onSubmit` decodes the values with the same schema to get the trimmed name.

items.name: step-indicator-tanstack-form
items.title: Step Indicator: TanStack Form
items.description:
Keep the step in React state and the values in TanStack Form. One Effect Schema describes the whole form; each step validates its field with the matching `Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(Signup.fields.name)` validator.

- **Mount every field.** `form.validateField` only finds validators on mounted fields, so an unmounted step would pass validation unchecked. Render all steps and hide the inactive ones with `field.TextField`'s `hidden`.
- **Validate only what the user passes.** `goTo` validates each step on the way forward, which also marks it touched, and stops at the first invalid one. Steps ahead are never validated, so they never show an error before the user reaches them.
- **Gate errors on `isTouched`.** The step's `invalid` uses `isTouched && !isValid`; the bound field shows its error under the same rule.
- **Submit validates everything.** `onSubmitInvalid` sends the user to the first failing step.
- Going back is always free.

items.name: typography-multilingual
items.title: Typography: Multilingual
items.description:
[Vazirmatn](https://github.com/rastikerdar/vazirmatn), created by [Saber Rastikerdar](https://github.com/rastikerdar), brings Arabic and Farsi into the same text hierarchy. These settings panels show the font in headings, descriptions, fields, and actions, alongside Latin project names.

We want to expand Erbium’s typography to support more languages and scripts. We believe AI has made internationalization easier, and everyone should be able to enjoy their apps in a language they know. That means making room for each script’s letterforms, reading direction, and spacing as we grow the system.

Set `lang` and `dir` at the content boundary. Arabic, Farsi, and Urdu keep the shared sizes but receive extra line height for their marks, each a whole pixel: 48px for display, 36px for title, 28px for subtitle and body, 24px for caption, and 22px and 20px for the two control sizes.

Keep natural letter spacing in Arabic-script text, avoid uppercase transformations, and use semibold emphasis rather than synthesized italics. Wrap mixed-direction identifiers and numbers in `bdi`; code blocks remain left-to-right. Try editing the fields and narrowing the preview to see how the text wraps.
